title: Reverse a String Recursively
statement:
Given a string `s`, return it reversed: the last character becomes the first, the second-to-last becomes the second, and so on.

The interviewer asked for a **recursive** solution, so implement it by recursion: the reverse of a string is the reverse of everything after its first character, followed by that first character, and the reverse of the empty string (or of a single character) is itself.

The string contains only letters and digits, and is read as a single token.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string `s` (no spaces).
outputFormat: Print the reversed string on one line.
constraints: `s` consists of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits
The recursion depth of the natural solution is at most |s| ≤ 5000

examples.explanation: Reversing `hello` gives `olleh`: reverse(`ello`) is `olle`, and appending the first character `h` gives `olleh`.
The characters in order are a, 1, B, 2; reading them from the end gives 2, B, 1, a.

hints: What is the reverse of an empty string, or of a one-character string? That is your base case.
If you already had the reverse of `s[1:]`, what single character would you append to finish the job?
Passing indices (or recursing from both ends and swapping) avoids creating a new substring on every call.
